Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def transform(grid):
    a=[r[:] for r in grid]; n=len(a); m=len(a[0])
    ones=[(r,c) for r in range(n) for c in range(m) if a[r][c]==1]
    r,c=min(ones)

    rr,cc=r,c
    hit=None
    while rr<n and cc<m:
        if grid[rr][cc]==2 and hit is None:
            hit=(rr,cc)
        a[rr][cc]=1
        rr+=1;cc+=1
    if hit:
        hr,hc=hit
        row=grid[hr]

        while right+1<m and row[right+1]==2:right+=1

            a[rr][cc]=1;rr+=1;cc-=1

            for dc in (-1,1):
                rr,cc=hr+1,hc+6

                    a[rr][cc]=1;rr+=1;cc+=dc

# General rule inferred from four pairs: long/short red bars launch 6-spaced rays, ending at next red bar.
def transform(grid):
    a=[row[:] for row in grid]; n=len(a); m=len(a[0])
    ones=sorted((r,c) for r in range(n) for c in range(m) if a[r][c]==1)
    r,c=ones[-1]
    trigger=None
    # red bar to the right of the last given diagonal cell
    if c+1<m and grid[r][c+1]==2:
        trigger=(r,c+1)
    else:
        rr,cc=r+1,c+1
        while rr<n and cc<m:
            if grid[rr][cc]==2:
                trigger=(rr,cc); break
            rr+=1;cc+=1
    # always extend primary diagonal until branching trigger/next red, or whole way without branch
    branch=False
    if trigger:
        tr,tc=trigger; row=grid[tr]; left=tc; right=tc
        while left and row[left-1]==2:left-=1
        while right+1<m and row[right+1]==2:right+=1
        L=right-left+1
        branch=L<=5 or L>=12
    rr,cc=r+1,c+1
    stop=trigger[0] if branch else n
    while rr<n and cc<m:
        a[rr][cc]=1;rr+=1;cc+=1
    if branch:
        tr,tc=trigger
        # stop all branched rays at next red bar
        nextred=n
        for rr in range(tr+1,n):
            if 2 in grid[rr]: nextred=rr;break
        starts=[(tc,1),(tc+6,1),(tc+6,-1),(tc+12,-1)]
        for sc,dc in starts:
            rr,cc=tr+1,sc
            while rr<nextred and 0<=cc<m:
                a[rr][cc]=1;rr+=1;cc+=dc
    return a
out3=transform(test)
out3
